# IAMOauthClientCredential

`iam.gcp.hfl.dev/v1alpha1`

**Gap it fills.** a credential (client secret) of a project's OAuth client for workforce identity federation (Terraform's `google_iam_oauth_client_credential`); in no Config Connector code or pull request (searched 2026-11-23); `docs/coverage/foundation.md` item 4.

**Source.** generated by `hack/discokind` from the IAM API's Discovery document

## Notes

The API returns the credential's `clientSecret` on every read. It never
goes to status: the controller writes it to a Kubernetes Secret in the
object's namespace, owned by the object, named by `spec.secretOutput.name`
(default the object's name), under the key `clientSecret`
(`docs/design.md` decision 38, the `hack/discokind` option
`secretOutputs`). A Secret that is lost is written again at the next
reconcile, from a read. A Secret of that name that the object does not own
is left alone, and the object is not Ready, before anything is made in the
cloud. The Secret goes with the object, through garbage collection, also
when the object is abandoned (`deletion-policy: abandon` keeps the
credential, not its Secret; a new object for it writes the Secret again).

The API asks that a credential be disabled before it is deleted ("Before
deleting an OauthClientCredential, it should first be disabled"), so a
delete first patches `disabled: true` (`disableBeforeDelete`); the fake
refuses a delete of an enabled credential, as the description says. A
live run shows whether the API refuses one.

`oauthClient` is the OAuth client's ID (an `IAMOauthClient`'s
`resourceID` or name); the credential's own ID is 4 to 32 characters, so
the fixtures set `resourceID` (`${SHORT_ID}`).

Tests: `TestIAMOauthClientCredential` (the generated kind test, which also
checks the Secret and that no value is in the object) and
`TestSecretOutputs` in `pkg/controller/direct/iam/discokindtest/`.

Generated by `hack/discokind` from `hack/discokind/kinds.yaml` and the
